research_question: How does an index fund differ from a mutual fund, and what separates index and active mutual funds in cost, pricing, and taxes?

research_brief.purpose: Explain that index is a strategy and mutual fund is a structure, and compare index and active mutual funds on verified data.
research_brief.data_period: FINRA guide and Vanguard fund pages checked October 26, 2026; Vanguard expense data as of April 28, 2026; industry averages as of December 31, 2025.
research_brief.scope_limitations: ICI asset-share data could not be verified (ici.org returned 403) and was removed. Fidelity FXAIX page did not render without scripts and was removed. No fund recommendation.

sources.title: Mutual Funds
sources.scope: Mutual fund structure, NAV pricing, active vs passive, fees, turnover, 12b-1, distributions
sources.verification_note: Quoted: open-end funds bought and redeemed daily at NAV; NAV calculated once a day when markets close; passive funds seek to replicate benchmarks; 12b-1 fees capped at 1 percent; transaction costs not in expense ratio.
